options: Limits the result to the first 10 rows, after whatever ordering is applied
Returns only rows where a column equals 10

questions.explain: TOP n caps the number of rows returned to n.

questions.q: Why does TOP almost always need to be paired with ORDER BY?
options: Without ORDER BY, row order isn't guaranteed, so 'the first 10 rows' is meaningless
TOP causes a syntax error without ORDER BY
ORDER BY makes TOP run faster, but isn't otherwise necessary
TOP only works on numeric columns, and ORDER BY fixes that
questions.explain: This directly follows from Lesson 17 — no ORDER BY means no guaranteed order, so TOP without it returns an undefined set of rows.

questions.q: On a table with 504 rows, what does TOP 10 PERCENT return?
options: 51 rows (10% of 504 rounded up)
Exactly 10 rows
50 rows exactly, always rounding down
504 rows — PERCENT is ignored without a WHERE clause
questions.explain: TOP PERCENT rounds up to the nearest whole row — 10% of 504 is 50.4, which rounds up to 51.

questions.q: Can TOP be combined with WHERE?
options: Yes — e.g. TOP 5 with WHERE Color = 'Red' finds the 5 most expensive red products
No, TOP and WHERE cannot appear in the same query
Only if WHERE comes after ORDER BY
TOP replaces WHERE entirely
questions.explain: TOP works alongside WHERE and ORDER BY together, filtering first and then capping the row count.

questions.q: What determines which specific rows TOP 10 returns?
options: The ORDER BY clause — TOP takes the first n rows after sorting
The order the rows were originally inserted, always
Alphabetical order of the table name
TOP always returns the 10 rows with the lowest primary key
questions.explain: TOP simply caps the row count from whatever order the query — via ORDER BY — actually produces.
